clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: Meet Cap, a drug molecule.

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: CYP3A4 is a liver enzyme that clears many medicines from the body.

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: Will Cap switch it off, and keep it off?

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: CYPMode answers this for two real tasks of the OpenADMET challenge.

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: 750 hidden molecules to classify, and 20 ligands to place in the enzyme.

clips.speaker: Kai
clips.text: I run the assay. Every compound is measured twice: at once, and after a head start with the enzyme.

clips.speaker: Kai
clips.text: The shift between the two is the label.

clips.speaker: Kai
clips.text: Kai measures every compound twice.

clips.speaker: Kai
clips.text: Cap's two measurements agree: the compound is not time-dependent.

clips.speaker: Kai
clips.text: Real data: every point is one compound of the challenge.

clips.speaker: Kai
clips.text: Above the line, the head start made the compound clearly stronger: that is the label.

clips.speaker: Scout
clips.text: I go through every file the organisers released and compare it, by compound name, with the blinded test set.

clips.speaker: Scout
clips.text: A compound of the test set is taken out before anything is computed.

clips.speaker: Scout
clips.text: Scout goes through every file the organisers released.

clips.speaker: Scout
clips.text: Only names are compared: the measurement of a test compound is never read.

clips.speaker: Scout
clips.text: Three of the six files hold test compounds, five in all. They are taken out first.

clips.speaker: Scout
clips.text: The organisers confirmed the overlap of the Octant release.

clips.speaker: Bits
clips.text: I turn molecules into numbers a model can read: which small groups of atoms are present, how big, how polar, how reactive.

clips.speaker: Bits
clips.text: 12,412 numbers for every compound.

clips.speaker: Bits
clips.text: Bits turns a real molecule into numbers.

clips.speaker: Bits
clips.text: A fingerprint records which small groups of atoms the molecule contains.

clips.speaker: Bits
clips.text: Descriptors record its size, its shape and how polar it is.

clips.speaker: Bits
clips.text: Together: 12,412 numbers describe every compound.

clips.speaker: Stacker
clips.text: I train 23 different models. Each votes on whether a compound switches an enzyme off for good.

clips.speaker: Stacker
clips.text: Then a logistic stack learns whom to trust and blends the votes into one score.

clips.speaker: Stacker
clips.text: Stacker's 23 models each cast a vote.

clips.speaker: Stacker
clips.text: A logistic stack learns whom to trust.

clips.speaker: Stacker
clips.text: Its ranking is checked on folds that no choice has seen.

clips.speaker: Stacker
clips.text: One score per compound: the highest are called positive.

clips.speaker: Gatekeeper
clips.text: Before an experiment runs, I write down the rule it must pass. Nothing is tuned until it passes.

clips.speaker: Gatekeeper
clips.text: Every idea is judged alone and inside the final blend.

clips.speaker: Gatekeeper
clips.text: Gatekeeper fixes the rule before the result exists.

clips.speaker: Gatekeeper
clips.text: Every idea the project tried is in the ledger.

clips.speaker: Gatekeeper
clips.text: Almost all of them ended "not met": the data did not support them.

clips.speaker: Quanta
clips.text: I computed orbitals and reactive sites with GFN2-xTB, atom by atom, for thousands of molecules.

clips.speaker: Quanta
clips.text: Quanta computed physics for every compound with GFN2-xTB.

clips.speaker: Quanta
clips.text: Some columns carry signal alone, but no physics idea passed its gate.

clips.speaker: Quanta
clips.text: Beautiful physics: honestly reported as not used.

clips.speaker: Foundry
clips.text: I start from models pretrained on millions of molecules and ask whether any of them improves the blend.

clips.speaker: Foundry
clips.text: Each one is added to the stack and judged by the same rule.

clips.speaker: Foundry
clips.text: Foundry starts from models pretrained on millions of molecules.

clips.speaker: Foundry
clips.text: Each one is added to the stack and judged by the same rule.

clips.speaker: Foundry
clips.text: 7 of the 7 judged so far did not pass.

clips.speaker: Foundry
clips.text: A model that adds nothing to the blend is reported as nothing.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: I fold each ligand into the enzyme with Boltz-2, restrain the nitrogen that can bind the iron, and check every pose.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: Two co-folding models work with me.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: Dock folds the molecule into the enzyme with Boltz-2.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: Some molecules bind the heme iron through a nitrogen: a Type II interaction.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: For some ligands the nitrogen is placed far from the iron, so Dock restrains it.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: On the crystal benchmark the restraint passed its pre-declared gate.

clips.speaker: Dock
clips.text: Every pose is checked with PoseBusters before it is handed in.

clips.speaker: Auditor
clips.text: I run the whole project twice and compare the two reports byte for byte.

clips.speaker: Auditor
clips.text: If one byte differs, the work is not reproducible and I say so.

clips.speaker: Auditor
clips.text: The Auditor runs everything twice.

clips.speaker: Auditor
clips.text: The two audit reports are identical, byte for byte.

clips.speaker: Auditor
clips.text: Tests, queue jobs and the final zip are all accounted for.

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: The results, estimated on the training data with nested cross-validation.

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: Nine specialists, one molecule, and every number read from the project's own files.

clips.speaker: Narrator
clips.text: The challenge closes on 3 November 2026.
